text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.24% today to close at $478.07, continuing a sharp two-week rally of 13.2%. The underlying driver is crude oil strength: U.S. oil is trading at $101.91 per barrel (up from around $75 two weeks ago), fueled by escalating Iran-related geopolitical risk in the Strait of Hormuz and shipping strikes that have pushed tanker rates dramatically higher. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with relatively tight crude and product inventories, which means Marathon can process this higher-priced oil into fuel and benefit from the margin.

The broader context is that physical oil delivery costs have spiked due to shipping disruptions—analysts note the true cost of delivered crude is roughly $30-40 higher than headline prices—and Middle Eastern supply uncertainty is supporting crude prices even as U.S. inventory levels remain adequate. This is a classic scenario where refiner margins can widen: Marathon buys expensive crude but sells refined products into a market where the delivery premium has made fuel valuable enough to offset the crude cost increase.
